claim: Simon Andriesz, 57, a British former managing director at BGC Partners, was found dead on September 23, 2026 in a town outside Bangkok, Thailand. BGC is the brokerage spun off from Cantor Fitzgerald, which Howard Lutnick ran before he became Commerce Secretary. His family said he took his own life. The Banker reported a suicide. The Daily Mail, citing a local municipal office, reported the listed cause as "asphyxiation from hanging"; other outlets said they could not independently verify that finding. Thai authorities have not publicly released an official cause of death. Andriesz had spent about a decade alleging misconduct at BGC. He won $500,000 against the firm in a June 2024 arbitration before FINRA (the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority, the US brokerage self-regulator), and the US Commodity Futures Trading Commission later paid him a whistleblower award of about $420,000. BGC said it had long disputed his allegations. He told the BBC he took allegations of undisclosed Lutnick–Epstein business dealings to the FBI in 2020 and 2021 and met "no interest." In the DOJ Epstein release, an FBI case-file serial index includes an entry titled with his name, dated February 16, 2021. It sits beside the April 2021 complaint form recording a 2020 tip about Lutnick, which was logged without a case being opened. A July 24, 2025 email in the release summarizing allegations against named figures lists his report under Lutnick's name. Searching the release, he flagged a May 2018 email in which Epstein asked Lutnick about the prospects of AdFin, a startup in which both Epstein and a Cantor venture arm had invested. He gave that correspondence to the House Oversight Committee before Lutnick's May 6, 2026 interview. In an August 9, 2026 post he wrote that the consequences of whistleblowing "have been devastating" and that he intended "to share more of the evidence and the story behind what happened." He had been wrongly told by the UK Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) that he did not qualify for whistleblower protection. After his death the FCA asked Lea Paterson, a newly appointed non-executive board member, to review how it dealt with him. A cross-party group of MPs said the regulator should not "mark its own homework" and called for an independent review. Lutnick has denied wrongdoing in connection with Epstein.

notes: Corpus-first: Andriesz is in our own release corpus 6x (DS10): EFTA01648946/EFTA01648951/EFTA01656173/EFTA01660622 (the July 24 2025 'named figures' allegation summary — a compilation of victim statements and NTOC tips, many unverified; only the Lutnick line is quoted here, NOT the victim allegations about others); EFTA01730634 (FBI 50D-NY-3027571 serial index, serial 593 'SIMON ANDRIES2 02.16.2021' — OCR '2' for 'Z'; adjacent serial 595 = the FD-71A in record 2021-lutnick-fbi-guardian-complaint-001); EFTA01684300 (serial-synopsis spreadsheet, column-truncated OCR: 'Simon Andriesz, date of birth[redacted]', 'Andriesz, call[i]ng from the United Kingdom, previously worked for BGC Financial (BGC) and Can[tor] Fitzgera[l]d (CF) in the financial market. Andriesz was responsible for reviewing reporting, and comp[liance]... Andriesz uncovered fraud, money laundering, Ponz[i] schemes, and regulat[ory]...', '...based on the possible location of Lutnick within the United States'). Redaction posture: the FD-71A in 2021-lutnick-fbi-guardian-complaint-001 redacts the complainant; this record does NOT assert that the redacted complainant is Andriesz — it reports only what the release states by name elsewhere (serial 593 title, the 2025 summary) and what Andriesz said publicly (he self-identified on X as 'the British whistleblower who reported evidence concerning Howard Lutnick'). The release's serial entries vs. Andriesz's 'no interest' account are set side by side; no conclusion drawn. Cause of death: family statement + The Banker + Daily Mail municipal citation (unverified by IBTimes); no Thai police/official cause published as of Oct 2026 — the suicide finding is attributed, not adopted. Post date: embedded tweet dated Aug 9 2026; some outlets framed it as a 'final post' surfacing in October. Commerce Dept told the BBC there was 'no evidence of wrongdoing' (via Newsmax/Yahoo).
